en: Dependent on a state with taints (*sāsava*), a state without taints (*anāsava*) arises by way of the root-condition (*hetupaccaya*).

Dependent on a state without taints, a state without taints arises by way of the root-condition. Dependent on a state without taints, a state that is neither-with-taints-nor-without-taints (*nasāsava*) arises by way of the root-condition. Dependent on a state without taints, a state that is neither-with-taints-nor-without-taints...
And with the root condition, both tainted (*sāsava*) and untainted (*anāsava*) phenomena arise.
Dependent on both tainted and untainted phenomena, an untainted phenomenon arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Under the root condition there are five;
under the object condition, two ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition, five. (The full detail applies everywhere.)
